summary: Bind optional named claim stores to a durable shard ID and reject replication exchanges addressed to another store.

replay.detail: No existing claim is replayed, moved, or deleted. The default store continues to omit the optional shard ID in exchanges.

schema.detail: An explicitly opened named store records its shard ID in its own meta table. Opening a used default store under a shard name or opening a named file under a different name fails before exchange admission.

rules.detail: Claim, projection, checkpoint, and retention rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Replication exchanges gain an optional shard_id field. Legacy and default exchanges omit it. A named store rejects an omitted or different ID; the default store rejects a named ID. No shard transport is wired by this change.

downtime.detail: No deployed shard opens or routes writes by default.

manual.detail: No operator action enables a shard. Activation and a one-member trial still require the reviewed topology choice and Ops binding.

recovery.detail: The shard marker persists across reopen. An empty-looking default file with fleet or checkpoint history cannot be relabelled as a shard; restore keeps each named file with its recorded ID.
